observations.text: The change is client-side but its effect is server-side. TIB-5460 changes the VALUE of the identity key that a server-side quota counter buckets on. Nothing in the SDK enforces the limit; the SDK only decides what identity is presented. Every high-severity consequence of this task therefore lands on a surface the knowledge base does not model (GAP-02, GAP-05), which is why the blast radius cannot be bounded by comparison.

observations.text: The two canonical checks the change most directly disturbs are not upload checks at all - they are page-load checks. CHK-023 asserts that NO teeinblue localStorage key exists at initial page load (keys appear only on first personalization interaction) and CHK-031 asserts ZERO XHR/fetch to teeinblue-owned hosts during personalization, with server sync only at add-to-cart. Fix part (b) writes a key at page load and fires a network request at page load. Both baselines become incomplete in scope even though neither check mentions upload.

The dev note's own verification step for fix part (b) is not discriminating while CTX-CONF-02 is open. translation/kb.json KB-017 recorded the thumbmark request firing on plain page load on 2026-09-21 - i.e. observing 'GET /thumbmark on page load' after the fix reproduces an observation that already existed before it. See payload.ctx_conf_02_carry_forward for what that leaves as usable evidence.
observations.source: CTXSLICE conflicts[CTX-CONF-02]; JIRA:TIB-5460 comment 51220 Test step 3

observations.text: The FEAT-07 regression radius is bundle-level, not mechanism-level. Of 38 published checks, exactly two (CHK-023, CHK-031) share a mechanism with the change; a third group (CHK-001, CHK-027, CHK-033/038) shares a lifecycle moment (page load / reload / which bundle is served). The remaining ~31 checks - variant + pricing, 2-level personalization dependency, grouped_clipart 2-step, inline validation, preview/mockup, cart line-item shape, multi-store publish pre-flight - have no path to ThumbmarkService and are covered adequately by one bundle smoke rather than by re-running them.

This is the second consecutive ticket to modify teeinblue-sdk ThumbmarkService, and the first ticket (TIB-5341) shipped the defect while its own Constraints said it would make no SDK change (CONF-03). That makes the predecessor's stated scope an unreliable boundary for judging what TIB-5460 can reach, and is an independent argument for re-running TIB-5341's own checks rather than trusting either ticket's scope statement.

payload.headline: HIGH blast radius. The change is three lines of client behaviour that together redefine the key of a server-side, money-spending quota, on a surface with ZERO regression baseline. Four layers are touched (storefront SDK, browser storage, backend API contract, portal config as applicability-only), two registry objects (sdk HIGH, artwork MEDIUM) plus campaign as test data, and two server-side code surfaces that have no knowledge object at all. The change is also the second consecutive ticket on ThumbmarkService/ValidateThumbmark, which per the rule library drags TIB-5341's own checks back into scope. The dominant risk is NOT the reported bug recurring - it is the opposite failure, an unstable random ID silently disabling rate limiting on paid AI calls, for which neither canonical context nor Jira supplies an oracle.

regression_surface.principle: Selection rule applied: a published check enters the regression surface only if it shares a MECHANISM (identity, page-load network, browser storage) or a LIFECYCLE MOMENT (page load, reload, bundle load) with the change. Sharing only the bundle is covered by ONE smoke check, not by re-running the bundle's whole checklist. 6 of 38 FEAT-07 checks qualify; the other 32 are listed as excluded with reasons.

in_scope.title: localStorage draft ('teeinblue-customizations'/'teeinblue-global-options') does NOT exist at initial load, created only on first personalization interaction
in_scope.why: Directly disturbed. After D-03/D-06 the SDK writes teeinblue_signed_thumbmark at page load, BEFORE any interaction. The check's own assertions about the two draft keys remain true, but its enumeration and the page-load storage picture it paints become wrong. A tester using it as the page-load storage baseline will misread the new key as an anomaly.

in_scope.title: Server sync (APIOP-051) only at Add-to-cart; ZERO XHR/fetch to teeinblue hosts while filling fields
in_scope.why: Directly disturbed, in two ways. (a) The page-load thumbmark request adds a teeinblue-host call to a page the baseline described as network-silent until ATC. (b) Worse for the check's letter: with an 8s timeout plus one retry (D-04/D-05), a retried thumbmark request can land ON the wire seconds into the field-filling window, i.e. inside the exact interval CHK-031 asserts is silent. Also the closest existing technique for the 'no SECOND fetch at upload' assertion (CR-09).

in_scope.title: Pass the password gate and the product page renders fully after publish (both stores)

If widget init awaits the fetch on a slow or blocked network, the failure shows up here first, as a slow or incomplete render, on every campaign page - not only on AI-effect ones.

regression_surface.regression_surface_verdict: 6 of 38 checks in scope; 2 of those (CHK-023, CHK-031) are directly disturbed by the change rather than merely adjacent. The honest summary is that the FEAT-07 regression surface is SMALL, and that this is bad news rather than good: the smallness is a symptom of GAP-04 (the buyer upload flow has no baseline at all), not evidence that the change is contained.

reasoning: SPAN: four layers, two registry objects (sdk HIGH, artwork MEDIUM) plus campaign as test data, and two server-side code surfaces (ValidateThumbmark, the quota counter) that the registry has no object for at all (GAP-05). A change whose consequences land where the knowledge model has no place to hold them cannot be rated lower than HIGH.

SEMANTICS: the change redefines the KEY of a shared server-side counter. The counter's code need not change for its observable behaviour to change completely (L4b). That is a bigger semantic move than the three-line client diff suggests.

BIDIRECTIONAL FAILURE: under-correction leaves real buyers blocked on their first upload (revenue loss, the reported symptom); over-correction - a random ID regenerated per page load - silently disables rate limiting on calls TIB-5341 records as carrying real $ cost. Both failure directions are live because D-06 (where the ID is persisted) is unstated. A change that can fail in opposite directions with the same code is high-radius by construction.

CROSS-TICKET: this is the SECOND consecutive ticket modifying teeinblue-sdk ThumbmarkService and the first to depend on TIB-5341's ValidateThumbmark acceptance rules. The rule library (rules/rate-limit-public-endpoints.md, via REQ RISK-08) requires re-running the predecessor's critical checks - legacy unsigned format still accepted (F41-02/F41-06), tampered signature returns 401 (F41-06), per-route buckets independent (F41-07). Two aggravators: (a) TIB-5341's own Constraints said it would make no SDK change yet it shipped the SDK fallback this ticket fixes (F41-08/CONF-03), so scope statements are not a reliable boundary; (b) Jira contains NO link between the two issues in either direction (TASK OBS-INTAKE-03/04), so the dependency is invisible to anyone not reading the QA rule library.

AMPLIFIER - NO BASELINE: the four core topics are MISSING from canonical context (GAP-01..GAP-04): 0 of 38 FEAT-07 checks upload anything, 'upload' appears 0 times in the FEAT-07 profile, 'visitor' appears 0 times in knowledge/, and the gap is not even listed among sdk kb.json's 21 declared coverage_gaps. Any post-fix upload observation is a FIRST observation, not a comparison - so the radius cannot be bounded by regression evidence, only by reasoning.

AMPLIFIER - UNOBSERVED POPULATION: all storefront knowledge is guest + desktop + US/USD/en (GAP-06, declared twice as a gap in sdk CHK-020 and artwork CHK-019). The bug's population is mobile, same device model/region, private browsing, shared carrier IP. The population most affected is exactly the one never observed.
AMPLIFIER - UNATTRIBUTABLE BUILD: no fixVersion, no PR, no commit (U-03), and which bundle each store serves is a P1 UNRESOLVED conflict (CTX-CONF-01). Nothing binds an observation to the fix.
what_would_LOWER_the_rating: A dev answer to U-IMP-01 confirming the random fallback ID is persisted, and where - this collapses the over-correction half of the bidirectional failure and removes the blocker on the highest-value assertion.
A dev answer to U-IMP-02 confirming the legacy-unsigned acceptance window is open on staging and production, with a closing date - this removes the 401-on-every-fallback-upload scenario (R-02).
A build/PR reference (U-03) plus a dev answer to CTX-CONF-02 - together these make observations attributable and make fix part (b) verifiable as a delta.
Confirmation that teeinblue-api was not touched (ASM-IMP-02) - this holds the API layer at contract exposure rather than changed code.
blast_radius_rating.what_does_NOT_lower_it: The small number of impacted published checks (6 of 38). That smallness reflects GAP-04, not containment.

risks.title: Over-correction: rate limiting silently disabled by an unstable random ID
risks.evidence_class: Reasoned from two CONFIRMED requirements that cannot both hold without an unstated mechanism
risks.reason: CR-01 requires the fallback ID to be unique per browser; CR-08 requires it to be stable across reloads within the window. Both hold only if the value is persisted (D-06), and no source says it is. In the private/incognito case the ticket itself highlights, the description says the ID 'may not be stored'. If the ID is regenerated per page load, every reload hands the visitor a fresh quota and the limit stops existing for anyone willing to press F5 - on calls TIB-5341 records as carrying real $ cost.
risks.blocked_by: U-IMP-01 (dev answer required). This risk cannot be turned into an acceptance assertion; REQ gate D1 already forbids writing one.

risks.title: ValidateThumbmark rejects the new unsigned random fallback -> 401 on every fallback upload
risks.evidence_class: Needs dev confirmation (sourced from TIB-5341, SUPPLEMENTARY)
risks.reason: The random fallback is unsigned. TIB-5341 made the server verify signatures and accept legacy unsigned values only during a soft-transition window (F41-02/F41-06). TIB-5460 never mentions that window. If it has closed, the fix converts 'some buyers blocked' into 'every fallback upload fails with 401' - strictly worse than the bug. Second-order: a 401 seen during the collision test will be misread as an SDK defect.
risks.oracle_available: Only from TIB-5341 (supplementary), and only as regression, never as TIB-5460 acceptance criteria.
risks.blocked_by: U-IMP-02 - must be answered BEFORE execution, not during.

risks.title: The collision fix does not actually work - or appears to work for the wrong reason
risks.reason: The core assertion: with the thumbmark endpoint blocked, two independent browser contexts must each get their own quota, so the second context's FIRST upload succeeds. Twin hazards: (a) two incognito windows of the same browser share a process and may share storage, so the setup may not faithfully simulate two customers (RISK-09); (b) a warm teeinblue_signed_thumbmark from earlier staging testing silently skips the fallback path altogether, producing a false PASS (RISK-05) - the dev note flags the stale key for step 3 only, but it poisons steps 1 and 2 just as badly.
risks.mitigation_note: Cache-clear must be a PRECONDITION on every fallback-path case, and the result should be corroborated with two different browsers or profiles, not two incognito windows of one browser.

risks.title: Page-load fetch changes the storefront page-load baseline and can degrade widget init
risks.reason: D-03/D-06 add a network call and a storage write to page load, invalidating the scope of CHK-023 and CHK-031 (BR-CHAIN-04). Beyond bookkeeping, the dev note's claim that an 8s timeout is 'safe since it's a background page-load fetch' is an untested assertion: if widget init awaits it, a blocked or slow network delays or breaks render on EVERY campaign page, including ones with no AI effect and no upload at all. That is the widest-reaching failure mode in this list.
risks.oracle_available: Partly - the CHK-001 render baseline exists; the 'is init blocked' question has no oracle.

risks.title: Fix part (b) inverts itself on shared-IP populations
risks.reason: Fetching at page load multiplies traffic to an endpoint throttled 30/min per IP (F41-01), whose limit this ticket explicitly declines to raise (CR-11). Office networks, carrier NAT and crawlers can exhaust it without anyone uploading; each exhausted visitor is pushed onto the fallback path - the opposite of part (b)'s intent. The dev note's own 'Known follow-up' concedes the exposure on CGNAT and defers it.
risks.suggested_evidence: One measurement, not a pass/fail: how many thumbmark requests a normal browsing session of N product pages generates.

risks.title: Retry policy implemented in the wrong direction (retry on 429, or retry more than once)
risks.evidence_class: Confirmed oracle (CR-03) - this is one of the few fully assertable items
risks.reason: A retry on 429 amplifies load against the endpoint's own IP-keyed limit, compounding R-05. 'No retry on 429' is stated explicitly and is unambiguously new behaviour, which also makes it one of the few signatures that can DISTINGUISH the fixed bundle from the old one (see ctx_conf_02_carry_forward).

risks.title: 'Previous processed images' (72h, per-buyer) orphaned by the identity change
risks.reason: sdk KB-027 records the portal toggle 'Allow buyers to choose previous processed images' enabled on both stores, with 72-hour help text. If that gallery is keyed on the visitor identity this task changes, a buyer whose fallback ID differs from their earlier one loses sight of their own processed images - a silent data-visibility regression with no check anywhere, and the clearest instance of the radius reaching a feature nobody modelled.

risks.title: The reported customer symptom persists after the fix, via the 50/hour-per-IP AI-route backstop
risks.reason: F41-03's IP backstop is untouched (D-08). Two buyers behind one carrier NAT can still block each other on a first upload. The suite must therefore claim to verify the COLLISION MECHANISM, not the end-to-end absence of the reported symptom - otherwise a customer re-report after this ships reads as a failed fix.
risks.note: This is a reporting/claim-scope risk as much as a product risk.

risks.title: Multi-tab race at page load
risks.reason: Moving the fetch to page load makes concurrent fetches from two tabs far more likely than the old fetch-on-first-upload timing did. Two tabs can interleave writes to teeinblue_signed_thumbmark or to the fallback value, producing two identities for one visitor (quota split) or a torn write.

risks.title: The bundle under test cannot be identified, so no result is attributable
risks.reason: No fixVersion, no PR, no commit (U-03), and CONFLICT-PORTAL-001 over which store serves which bundle is UNRESOLVED at P1 with three mutually inconsistent evidence sides. Ranked as a process risk rather than a product risk because it does not break buyers - it breaks the claim that anything was verified.
risks.constraint_honoured: No per-store SDK-version claim is made in this artifact.

risks.title: TIB-5341 regression debt on the shared components
risks.evidence_class: Confirmed requirement from the rule library; oracle is supplementary
risks.reason: Second ticket on ThumbmarkService/ValidateThumbmark triggers re-running the predecessor's checks: legacy unsigned still accepted (F41-02), tampered signature -> 401 (F41-06), per-route buckets independent (F41-07). Ranked below R-02 because R-02 is the subset of this that can actively break the fix; the rest is genuine regression.
risks.oracle_available: From JIRA:TIB-5341 only, labelled SUPPLEMENTARY - must be marked as such and confirmed with dev before being treated as acceptance criteria for TIB-5460.

risks.title: GenAI paths may double-count, or may not be reachable by an 'upload' limit at all
risks.reason: Text-to-Image GENERATES rather than uploads an image (artwork KB-019's own note), so whether an upload rate limit reaches it is unanswered - yet comment 51220 lists Text-to-Image among the rate-limited AI effects. Separately, global-option KB-031 names a customer-uploads/generate path with status polling that may share the counter, so a GenAI effect could be a second hit against a quota whose identity mechanism just changed.
risks.constraint: KB-031 sits in an UNPUBLISHED object at 1 sample; used to raise the question only.

ctx_conf_02_carry_forward.status: OPEN - carried forward, not resolved (contract §8). Recorded as IMP-CONF-01.
ctx_conf_02_carry_forward.restatement: translation/kb.json KB-017 (OBSERVED_CURRENT, MEDIUM, observed_count 2, observed_at 2026-09-21, published CTX-20260921-02) recorded the thumbmark request firing on a plain product page load, across two page loads. Comment 51220 (created 2026-09-17, last edited 2026-09-18) presents fetch-at-page-load as new in TIB-5460.
three_live_readings_inherited_from_the_r: (a) the 2026-09-21 observation was already made against a post-fix bundle on staging;
(b) fetch-at-page-load is not as new as comment 51220 implies (it may predate the ticket);
(c) the observation is of a different trigger that happens to look like page load.
what_it_implies_for_verifying_fix_part_b: The POSITIVE half of dev Test step 3 - 'you should see a request to /merchant/{platform}/thumbmark fire immediately on page load' - is NOT DISCRIMINATING. Canonical context already recorded that same observation twice, two days ago, with no known connection to this fix. Observing it again after the fix confirms nothing about the delta, only about the current state. Any test case built solely on it would be an OBSERVED_CURRENT restatement dressed as verification.

Evidence that IS discriminating, in descending strength: (1) the NEGATIVE half of step 3 - after the page-load fetch succeeds, an upload must fire NO second GET /thumbmark (CR-09) - which is a statement about the upload-time path that KB-017 says nothing about; (2) the retry/timeout signature from D-04/D-05 - an 8s ceiling and exactly one retry on 5xx with zero retries on 429 - which is unambiguously new behaviour and observable in DevTools; (3) the fallback-ID shape itself (random vs device-derived), which is the actual fix and is independent of timing.

Therefore fix part (b) should be verified through CR-09 plus the resilience signature, and the page-load observation recorded as CORROBORATING STATE, explicitly annotated with KB-017 so nobody later reads it as proof of the delta.

The cheap resolution is external, not analytical: a build/PR reference (U-03) binding the 2026-09-21 staging bundle to pre- or post-fix code would collapse readings (a) and (b) immediately. That is one question to dev, and it also resolves R-10. It is the single highest-leverage question in this run.
ctx_conf_02_carry_forward.explicitly_not_done: This agent did not choose between (a), (b) and (c), did not edit translation/kb.json, and did not downgrade comment 51220's claim. The conflict travels forward to gen-testcase and to the orchestrator's KCP triage attached to BC-02.
